questions.question: If Dev can make 40 chairs in 20 days, working 10 hours per day then in how many days can he make 10 chairs working 8 hours per day?
questions.solution:
Working 10 hours per day Dev can make 40 chairs in 20 days

⇒ Working 1 hour per day Dev can make 4 chairs in 20 days

⇒ Working 8 hours per day Dev can make 32 chairs in 20 days

⇒ Working 8 hours per day Dev can make 1 chair in 20/32 days

⇒ Working 8 hours per day Dev can make 10 chairs in 20/32 × 10 days

∴ The required time to make 10 chairs is 6(1)/(4) days. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Formula Used:**

 MDH/W = constant

M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂

**Calculation:**

Let the work will be completed in x days

20 × 10/40 = x × 8/10

⇒ x = 20 × 10 × 10/(40 × 8)

⇒ x = 100/16 = 6(1)/(4)

∴ The required time to make 10 chairs is 6(1)/(4) days.

questions.question: A took 10 minutes more than B in covering a certain distance. If their speeds are in the ratio 3 : 4, then what is the time taken by B to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
Let the time taken by B to cover a distance S be x minutes

So, the time taken by A to cover the same distance S is (x + 10) minutes

Let the speed of A and B be 3v and 4v respectively 

Now, according to question

S = 3v × (x + 10) ----(i)

And S = 4v × x ----(ii)

On solving (i) and (ii), we get

3v × (x + 10) = 4v × x

⇒ 3x + 30 = 4x 

⇒ x = 30 minutes

∴ The time taken by to cover the same distance is 30 minutes

questions.question: Ajay sold an article for Rs. 84 at a loss of 30%. If he sells same article at Rs. 120, then what will be his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of the article be Rs. x 

Now, according to question

x × 70% = 84

⇒ x × 7/10 = 84

⇒ x = 120

So, the cost price of the article is Rs. 120

Since, new selling price is also Rs. 120

∴ There is no profit and no loss in this transaction

questions.question: Two articles were sold for Rs. 2400 each by a shopkeeper. The shopkeeper incurred no Profit and no loss on the whole transaction. If one of the two articles sold at profit of 20%, then what was the loss incurred on the other article?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of first and second articles are x and y respectively 

Total selling price of two articles is Rs. 4800

So, the total cost price of the two articles is also Rs. 4800 due to no loss and no gain

Now, according to question 

x × 120% = 2400

⇒ x × 6/5 = 2400

⇒ x = 2000

So, 2000 + y = 4800

⇒ y = 2800

Now, the loss occurred on second article = 2800 – 2400

∴ The loss occurred on second article is Rs. 400

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

When SP of two articles were same, then the net profit and loss will be

x + y + (xy/100) [In case of Loss, one element will be having negative value]

Don't take the loss value as 20%

Here the loss is 16.667%

20 + (-16.667) + (2 × 16.667/100) gives the value "0".

That means the loss on the other article will be 16.667 or 16(2/3)%

16(2/3)% = 1/6

Loss on the other article = 2400 × 1/6 = Rs. 400

questions.question: The ratio (by volume) of milk and water in a mixture is 2 : 1. If we add 12 litres of water in the mixture, then the ratio of milk and water becomes 4 :3. What is the quantity of water in the new mixture?
questions.solution:
Let the quantity of milk and water in the mixture are 2x and x respectively

After adding water in the mixture, the quantity of water in the mixture will be (x + 12)

According to question, 

2x/(x + 12) = 4/3

⇒ 6x = 4(x + 12)

⇒ 6x = 4x + 48

⇒ 2x = 48

⇒ x = 24

So, the quantity of water in the new mixture = 24 + 12 = 36

∴ The quantity of water in the new mixture will be 36 litres.

questions.question: If V₁ : V₂ = 1 : 2 and V₁ + V₂ = 147, then what is the value of V₂ – V₁?
questions.solution:
Given, V₁ : V₂ = 1 : 2 and V₁ + V₂ = 147

Let V₁ = x and V₂ = 2x

So, x + 2x = 147

⇒ 3x = 147

⇒ x = 49

⇒ V₁ = 49, V₂ = 2 × 49 = 98

⇒ V₂ – V₁ = 98 – 49

∴ The required difference is 49

questions.question: The average age of a group of 20 men is 30 years. A 50 years old man leaves the group, while a woman joins the group. The average age decreases by 1 year. What is the age of the woman?
questions.solution:
Let the age of woman be x years

According to question,

The sum of ages of 20 men = 20 × 30 = 600

Again, according to question

The sum of ages 19 men including 1 woman = 20 × 29

⇒ 600 – 50 + x = 20 × 29

⇒ 550 + x = 580

⇒ x = 30

∴ The age of woman is 30 years

questions.question: If the lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 18 cm, then what is the area of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 18 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of rhombus = 1/2 × d1 × d2

where d1 and d2 are the diagonals of the rhombus

**Calculation:**

So, the area of rhombus = 1/2 × 24 × 18

**∴ The area of rhombus is 216 cm²**

questions.question: The average of 36, 28, 43, 56, 74, 65, 12 and x is 45. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 36, 28, 43, 56, 74, 65, 12 and x is 45.

Concept used:

Total = Number of entities × Average

**Calculation:**

(36 + 28 + 43 + 56 + 74 + 65 + 12 + x)/8 = 45

⇒ 314 + x = 360

⇒ x = 360 – 314

**∴ The value of x is 46.**

questions.question: What is the area of the largest square which can be inscribed in a circle of radius 28 cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of circle = 28cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/022e7cbb5568c1a502bf2bd61b0648f5d2a987d27a0ae30becfb8c5a0e6c725e.png] 

We know that the diagonal of the square which can be inscribed in a circle is equal to the diameter of the circle

So, the diagonal of square = 28 × 2 = 56 cm

⇒ √2 × a = 56, where a is the length of the side of the square

⇒ a = 28√2

So, the area of square = a²

The area of the square = (28√2)²

**∴ The area of the square is 1568 cm²**

questions.question: C and D together can make a chair in 4 days and C alone can make this chair in 12 days. In how many days D alone can make this chair?
questions.solution:
Since, the work done by (C + D) together in 1 day is 1/4 part of the total work

And the work done by C in one day is 1/12

So, the work done by D in one day = 1/4 – 1/12 = 1/6

∴ D alone can finish the whole work in 6 days

questions.question: A train moves at the speed of 80 km/h and crosses a platform in 0.75 minutes. If the length of the train is equal to the length of the platform, then what is the length of the platform?
questions.solution:
Let the length of train and the length of platform be x m

Now, according to question

2x = (80 × 5/18) × (0.75 × 60)

⇒ 2x = 1000

⇒ x = 500 m

∴ The length of platform is 500 m

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 900 is invested at compound interest (compounded annually) for 2 years. If the rate of interest is 10% per annum, then what will be the amount?
questions.solution:
Since, Amount = p × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

So, Amount = 900 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ Amount = 900 × 121/100

∴ The amount after two year will be Rs. 1089

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for two years is Rs. 1000 at the rate of 10% per annum. What is the amount after these two years?
questions.solution:
Since, we know that

Simple interest = P × R × T/100

⇒ 1000 = P × 10 × 2/100

⇒ P = 5000

Amount = Principal + S.I

So, the amount = 5000 + 1000

∴ The mount will be Rs. 6000
